title: Boundaries
description: Finding lower or upper bounds in sorted space.
identify: Looking for a transition point in a sorted array or monotonic search space
Problems asking for 'first index where condition holds' or 'last index where condition holds'
When the search space can be logically split into two halves of opposite boolean results (e.g., FFF...TTT)
appearsIn: LeetCode 34: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
explanation:
The Boundaries pattern is used to find the exact transition point in a sorted search space. This space can be conceptualized as having **opposite polarity**: it is partitioned into a range that fails a predicate condition and a range that passes it (e.g., `[False, False, False, True, True, True]`). By checking the midpoint `mid`:
1. If `condition(mid)` is `True` (positive polarity), it means `mid` is a valid candidate. However, since we want the *first* transition, a better candidate might exist to its left. Thus, we record `mid` as the candidate and search the left half (`high = mid - 1`).
2. If `condition(mid)` is `False` (negative polarity), the first transition must be strictly to the right of `mid`. Thus, we search the right half (`low = mid + 1`).

This systematic polarity partitioning ensures we never get stuck in infinite loops and can solve all boundary/transition problems with `O(log N)` complexity.

title: Rotated Sorted Array
description: Searching in arrays that have been shifted.
identify: Array is sorted but rotated around an unknown pivot point
Contains a discontinuity point where the ascending order breaks (e.g. `[4, 5, 6, 0, 1, 2]`)
Binary search midpoint divides the array into at least one fully sorted half
appearsIn: LeetCode 33: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
LeetCode 81: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II (with duplicates)
LeetCode 153: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
explanation: In a Rotated Sorted Array, at least one of the two halves partitioned by the midpoint `mid` is guaranteed to be fully sorted. We can leverage this by identifying which side is sorted, and checking if our target (or candidate) lies within that sorted range. This allows us to safely discard half of the search space at each iteration, maintaining the logarithmic `O(log N)` complexity.

title: Peak Elements
identify: Monotonically increasing then decreasing sequence (or vice-versa)
Finding local extrema (local maxima or local minima) in an unsorted or semi-sorted array/matrix
Using neighbor values to determine which direction the peak lies
appearsIn: LeetCode 852: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
LeetCode 1901: Find a Peak Element II
explanation: The Peak Elements pattern uses binary search on unsorted arrays by analyzing local slope directions. The core principle is that if `arr[mid] > arr[mid + 1]`, we are on a descending slope, which guarantees that a peak exists on the left (including `mid`). Conversely, if `arr[mid] < arr[mid + 1]`, we are on an ascending slope, which guarantees that a peak exists strictly on the right. This property allows us to discard half of the search space at each step, achieving `O(log N)` complexity for 1D arrays, and `O(M log N)` for 2D matrices.

title: BS on Answers (min/max)
description: Binary searching the answer space for direct values.
identify: Looking for the minimum possible value of some maximum constraint, or maximum of a minimum constraint
The search space has a clear, monotonic range [low, high] (e.g. [1, max_element] or [max_element, sum_elements])
A helper function possible(mid) can evaluate if a candidate value mid is feasible in O(N) time
appearsIn: LeetCode 1482: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
LeetCode 1283: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
LeetCode 1011: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
explanation: The Binary Search on Answers pattern is used to find an optimal value (minimum or maximum) from a continuous search space. Instead of searching over array indices, we binary search over the range of possible answers `[low, high]`. At each step, a helper function `possible(mid)` evaluates if the candidate `mid` is feasible. If it is, we record the candidate and continue to search for a more optimal value on one side; otherwise, we search on the opposite side. This reduces the search complexity to `O(N log(high - low))`.

title: BS on Answers (min(max) or max(min))
description: Binary searching the answer space for optimized boundaries.

title: BS on Partitions
description: Binary searching partitions across multiple arrays.
